Average BMI by Income Group, NHANES 1999-2023

Briefing dashboard for the community health board

The question

Has average BMI among adults age 20-80 in one income group gone up, gone down, or stayed about the same across NHANES survey cycles from 1999-2000 to 2021-2023? The board can use this to decide whether a follow-up analysis is worth asking for.

Income group shown: Low Income (<1.3). Versions for the other income groups (High Income (>3.5) and Middle Income) can be made on request.

What this shows

In this dataset, mean BMI for the Low Income (<1.3) group was 28.8 in 1999-2000 and 30.4 in 2021-2023. Each cycle includes at least 1,089 adults. This is a description of the pattern over time, not an explanation of why it happened. It can help the board decide what to ask next, for example whether the same pattern shows up in the other income groups.

Limitation

These are unweighted, descriptive averages from a classroom copy of NHANES. They do not account for the NHANES survey design, do not estimate BMI for U.S. adults, and do not show that income causes BMI.

Data and privacy

Data come from a cached classroom snapshot (nhanes_equity_v6) prepared from CDC/NCHS public-use NHANES files. The dashboard shows group averages only, never individual records.
